# @moku-labs/native — Full LLM Reference

> Node-only native packager framework for Moku, built on @moku-labs/core (Layer 2). It
> generates a gitignored Tauri 2 project under `projectDir` (default `.moku/tauri`),
> codegens the permission surface (Tauri capabilities JSON, the Info.ios.plist sidecar,
> AndroidManifest needs) from whichever system plugins the consumer app composed in
> `config.system`, and drives `tauri build` / `tauri ios|android build` for five targets:
> macos, windows, linux, ios, android. Package manager: bun exclusively. A real `node`
> binary on PATH is a hard prerequisite (`@tauri-apps/cli` cannot run under bun).

Version: 0.1.0. Dependencies: @moku-labs/common 0.3.0, @moku-labs/core 1.5.0, @tauri-apps/cli ^2.
Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.3.14. TypeScript strict with exactOptionalPropertyTypes and noUncheckedIndexedAccess.

Table of contents:
1. Architecture and initialization order
2. Global Config + Events (src/config.ts — verbatim types)
3. Config schema (every field: type, default, description)
4. Complete event catalog
5. project plugin (types + behavior)
6. tauri plugin (types + behavior)
7. build plugin (types + behavior)
8. doctor plugin (types + behavior)
9. cli plugin (types + behavior)
10. Public exports (src/index.ts)
11. Usage examples (incl. the two-createApp consumer composition)
12. Error handling patterns
13. Extension patterns (custom plugins)
14. Key design decisions
15. Signing, store builds, and the iOS simulator
16. Breaking changes in this release

====================================================================
1. ARCHITECTURE AND INITIALIZATION ORDER
====================================================================

Three-layer Moku model:
- Layer 1 — src/config.ts: `createCoreConfig<Config, Events, [typeof logPlugin, typeof envPlugin]>("native", { config: defaultConfig, plugins: [logPlugin, envPlugin], pluginConfigs: { env: { providers: [workerSafeProcessEnv()] } } })`. The two @moku-labs/common core plugins put `ctx.log` (structured logging, MC2) and `ctx.env` (validated env access, MC3) on every plugin context. The env PROVIDER is seeded here on purpose: the core plugin ships with zero providers, which left `ctx.env.get("PATH")` undefined and the tauri plugin with nothing to PATH-walk for `node`.
- Layer 2 — src/index.ts: `createCore(coreConfig, { plugins: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin] })`. NO `pluginConfigs` block: each plugin's defaults live in its own `src/plugins/<name>/index.ts`, so there is exactly one place per default.
- Layer 3 — consumer: `createApp({ config, plugins?, pluginConfigs? })` returns an app with `start()`/`stop()`, every plugin API surface (`app.project`, `app.tauri`, `app.build`, `app.doctor`, `app.cli`), and the core APIs (`app.log`, `app.env`).

Plugin dependency graph (D-007) and registration/initialization order:

  Wave 1 (dependency-free):   project        tauri
                                 ^  ^          ^  ^
  Wave 2:            build ------+--+----------+  |
                     doctor -----+-----------------+
                       ^  ^        (build -> [project, tauri])
                       |  |        (doctor -> [project, tauri])
  Wave 3:            cli -> [project, tauri, build, doctor]

Registration order in src/index.ts: project, tauri, build, doctor, cli.
- project and tauri never call each other; build orchestrates them; doctor reads them; cli fronts all four via ctx.require.
- Only project has an onInit (composition-time global-config validation — single owner).
- No plugin has onStart/onStop. tauri deliberately has NO onStop (D-002): a regular plugin's onStop receives only `{ global }` (no state/require/core APIs), so dev teardown is owned by the dev seam's own control flow (process-group spawn, SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, DevHandle.stop()) — which also covers Ctrl-C, where onStop would never fire.

Subprocess-seam ownership: tauri is the ONLY plugin that spawns processes for @tauri-apps/cli. doctor has its own `probeImpl` seam for non-tauri binaries (rustup/node/xcodebuild/xcodegen/pod/security/java/...), but its one tauri-CLI probe goes through `tauri.getVersion()` (D-013 ownership boundary).

Shared cross-plugin types: `MobileTarget`, `TauriRunner` and `BuildFlavor` are declared ONCE in src/config.ts and imported by the plugins' own `types.ts`. A plugin context is core's `PluginCtx<Config, State, Events>` intersected with what the plugin really uses, and `require` is constrained to that plugin's real dependencies — no mirror of core's internal types.

====================================================================
2. GLOBAL CONFIG + EVENTS (src/config.ts — verbatim)
====================================================================

/** The five packaging targets shipped in v1. */
export const TARGETS = ["macos", "windows", "linux", "ios", "android"] as const;

/** A native packaging target. */
export type Target = (typeof TARGETS)[number];

/**
 * Resolves the packaging targets a host can build with no extra opt-in — the default
 * `config.targets`. darwin -> ["macos"], win32 -> ["windows"], linux -> ["linux"],
 * any other host -> []. Mobile is NEVER inferred: ios/android need an SDK the host may
 * not have, so a consumer asks for them explicitly.
 */
export function hostTargets(platform: NodeJS.Platform): readonly Target[];

/** Pipeline phases in execution order — drives NativePhase and progress rendering. */
export const PHASE_ORDER = [
  "scaffold",
  "codegen",
  "icons",
  "compile",
  "bundle",
  "collect"
] as const;

/** A build pipeline phase. */
export type NativePhase = (typeof PHASE_ORDER)[number];

/**
 * Per-capability packaging parameters — ONE map drives both `Config["capabilities"]`
 * and project's `resolve<K extends keyof CapabilityConfigMap>`.
 * deep-link is custom-scheme-only in v1 (D-011); the `mode` discriminant keeps `"universal"` additive later.
 */
export type CapabilityConfigMap = {
  store: Record<string, never>;
  notification: Record<string, never>;
  "clipboard-manager": Record<string, never>;
  tray: Record<string, never>;
  "deep-link": { mode: "scheme"; scheme: string };
};

/** How `tauri ios build` exports the signed archive (`--export-method`). */
export type AppleExportMethod = "app-store-connect" | "release-testing" | "debugging";

/**
 * Apple signing identifiers for macOS and iOS builds — identifiers only, never secrets.
 * Credentials stay in the environment and Tauri reads them itself: APPLE_ID,
 * APPLE_PASSWORD, APPLE_TEAM_ID, APPLE_API_KEY, APPLE_API_ISSUER, APPLE_API_KEY_PATH,
 * APPLE_CERTIFICATE, APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD.
 */
export type AppleSigning = {
  teamId?: string;                    // bundle.iOS.developmentTeam
  signingIdentity?: string;           // bundle.macOS.signingIdentity; "-" means ad-hoc
  providerShortName?: string;         // bundle.macOS.providerShortName
  entitlements?: string;              // consumer entitlements plist, relative to cwd
  appStore?: boolean;                 // generate a sandbox entitlements file when `entitlements` is unset
  exportMethod?: AppleExportMethod;   // tauri ios build --export-method
  macosMinimumSystemVersion?: string;
  iosMinimumSystemVersion?: string;
};

/** Signing configuration — env-var REFERENCES and config-safe identifiers only, never raw secrets. */
export type SigningConfig = {
  apple?: AppleSigning;
  android?: {
    keystorePath?: string;
    keystorePasswordEnv?: string;
    keyPasswordEnv?: string;          // falls back to keystorePasswordEnv when unset
    keyAlias?: string;
  };
  windows?: { certificateThumbprint?: string };
};

/** Global configuration shape for the framework. Read by every plugin via `ctx.global`. */
export type Config = {
  /**
   * App identity and store metadata — project.onInit validates name/identifier are
   * non-empty (reverse-DNS identifier). `icon` is a 1024x1024 PNG relative to cwd
   * (a placeholder is generated when unset); `category` maps to `bundle.category`;
   * `buildNumber` maps to the iOS/macOS `bundleVersion`.
   */
  app: {
    name: string;
    identifier: string;
    version?: string;
    icon?: string;
    category?: string;
    buildNumber?: string;
  };
  /** Web build/dev wiring codegenned into tauri.conf.json. cwd for monorepo layouts. */
  web: { build: string; devCommand: string; devUrl: string; dist: string; cwd?: string };
  /** Composed `@moku-labs/system` plugins — the kernel-guaranteed name-only contract. */
  system: ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }>;
  /** Per-capability packaging parameters. */
  capabilities: Partial<CapabilityConfigMap>;
  /** Targets this app ships (default: the host's own desktop target — see hostTargets). */
  targets: readonly Target[];
  /** Generated Tauri project root (contains src-tauri/). Gitignored build output. */
  projectDir: string;
  /** Installer delivery root. */
  outDir: string;
  /** Signing env-var references. */
  signing: SigningConfig;
};

/** native:phase payload — one flat event, target as a field. */
export type NativePhaseEvent = {
  target: Target;
  phase: NativePhase;
  status: "start" | "progress" | "done" | "error";
  durationMs?: number;
  detail?: string;
};

/** native:complete payload — where the shippable artifacts landed. */
export type NativeCompleteEvent = {
  target: Target;
  outPath: string;
  artifacts: readonly string[];
  durationMs: number;
};

/** Framework-level events — emitted by build, hookable by all plugins (D-003). */
export type Events = {
  "native:phase": NativePhaseEvent;
  "native:complete": NativeCompleteEvent;
};

/** Shapes shared by several plugins — declared once here, never re-derived per plugin. */
export type MobileTarget = Extract<Target, "ios" | "android">;
export type TauriRunner = { nodePath: string; tauriJsPath: string };
export type BuildFlavor = { simulator?: boolean | undefined; aab?: boolean | undefined };

Framework default config literal (src/config.ts):

const defaultConfig: Config = {
  app: { name: "", identifier: "" },
  web: {
    build: "bun run build",
    devCommand: "bun run dev",
    devUrl: "http://localhost:5173",
    dist: "dist"
  },
  system: [],
  capabilities: {},
  targets: hostTargets(process.platform),
  projectDir: ".moku/tauri",
  outDir: "dist-native",
  signing: {}
};

src/config.ts also exports `coreConfig`, and the JSDoc-surviving explicit re-exports:
`export const createPlugin = coreConfig.createPlugin;`
`export const createCore = coreConfig.createCore;`

====================================================================
3. CONFIG SCHEMA (field-by-field)
====================================================================

GLOBAL Config (D-005 — the substantive surface; every plugin reads it via ctx.global):

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| app.name | string | "" | Display name (productName). Required: project.onInit throws when empty. |
| app.identifier | string | "" | Reverse-DNS bundle identifier (e.g. "com.example.myapp"). Validated against /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9-]*)+$/i. |
| app.version | string? | (absent -> "0.1.0" in tauri.conf.json) | Marketing version. |
| app.icon | string? | (absent) | Path to a 1024x1024 PNG, relative to cwd. Absent => a placeholder PNG is generated into projectDir. |
| app.category | string? | (absent) | Store category -> bundle.category. Key is ABSENT from the JSON when unset. |
| app.buildNumber | string? | (absent) | Store build number -> bundle.iOS.bundleVersion + bundle.macOS.bundleVersion. |
| web.build | string | "bun run build" | Web build command -> tauri.conf.json build.beforeBuildCommand `{ script, cwd }`. Required non-empty. |
| web.devCommand | string | "bun run dev" | Web dev command -> build.beforeDevCommand `{ script, cwd }`. Required non-empty. |
| web.devUrl | string | "http://localhost:5173" | Dev server URL — also DevHandle.url and the readiness-poll target. Required non-empty. |
| web.dist | string | "dist" | Web build output; resolved from web.cwd and rebased onto src-tauri as build.frontendDist (POSIX separators). Required non-empty. |
| web.cwd | string? | (absent => the process cwd) | Root of the web package (monorepo layouts). Both before-commands carry it explicitly, frontendDist resolves from it, and doctor's web-script/versions checks read package.json from it. |
| system | ReadonlyArray<{ name: string }> | [] | The composed system plugins — the shared cross-team contract. Unknown names throw at composition time. |
| capabilities | Partial<CapabilityConfigMap> | {} | Per-capability packaging parameters. "deep-link" in `system` REQUIRES capabilities["deep-link"] = { mode: "scheme", scheme } with a non-empty scheme. |
| targets | readonly Target[] | hostTargets(process.platform) | Targets this app ships; the default scope for build.runAll and doctor.run. ONE desktop target per host; ios/android are opt-in. |
| projectDir | string | ".moku/tauri" | Generated Tauri project root (contains src-tauri/). GITIGNORED build output, fully regenerable, never committed. |
| outDir | string | "dist-native" | Installer delivery root; collect copies artifacts to outDir/<target>/. |
| signing.apple.teamId | string? | (absent) | Apple Developer team id -> bundle.iOS.developmentTeam. |
| signing.apple.signingIdentity | string? | (absent) | Codesign identity -> bundle.macOS.signingIdentity ("-" = ad-hoc). |
| signing.apple.providerShortName | string? | (absent) | Multi-team notarization provider -> bundle.macOS.providerShortName. |
| signing.apple.entitlements | string? | (absent) | Consumer entitlements plist relative to cwd -> bundle.macOS.entitlements, rebased onto src-tauri. |
| signing.apple.appStore | boolean? | (absent) | true + no `entitlements` + macos target => generate src-tauri/Entitlements.plist (app-sandbox + network-client) and point bundle.macOS.entitlements at it. |
| signing.apple.exportMethod | AppleExportMethod? | (absent) | Read by the build plugin and passed to `tauri ios build --export-method` on DEVICE builds. |
| signing.apple.macosMinimumSystemVersion | string? | (absent) | -> bundle.macOS.minimumSystemVersion. |
| signing.apple.iosMinimumSystemVersion | string? | (absent) | -> bundle.iOS.minimumSystemVersion. |
| signing.android.keystorePath | string? | (absent) | Path to the release keystore (config-safe identifier). Absent => the Gradle signing block is REMOVED. |
| signing.android.keystorePasswordEnv | string? | (absent) | NAME of the env var holding the keystore password — a reference, never the secret. |
| signing.android.keyPasswordEnv | string? | (absent => keystorePasswordEnv) | NAME of the env var holding the key password. |
| signing.android.keyAlias | string? | (absent) | Key alias inside the keystore. |
| signing.windows.certificateThumbprint | string? | (absent) | Windows signing certificate thumbprint. |

PER-PLUGIN configs (minimal knobs/seams; overridable via createApp({ pluginConfigs })):

tauri (src/plugins/tauri/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| spawnImpl | SpawnFn \| undefined | undefined | Injectable spawn for tests; undefined => real detached process-group spawn. |
| nodePath | string \| undefined | undefined | Explicit node binary path; undefined => PATH-walk resolution over `ctx.env.get("PATH")` (never process.execPath, which is bun). |
| arch | NodeJS.Architecture \| undefined | undefined | Host arch the iOS simulator slice is derived from (x64 => `x86_64`, else `<arch>-sim`); undefined => process.arch. Pin it in tests so an argv assertion is host-independent. |
| readiness | { intervalMs: number; timeoutMs: number } | { intervalMs: 250, timeoutMs: 60_000 } | dev()'s devUrl poll cadence — no stdout "ready" marker exists (tauri#4740). |

doctor (src/plugins/doctor/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| probeImpl | ProbeFn \| undefined | undefined | Injectable probe runner for tests; undefined => real which/--version subprocess probes. The one tauri-CLI probe goes through tauri.getVersion() instead (D-013). |
| probeTimeoutMs | number | 10_000 | Per-check budget, twice over: handed to spawn as its `timeout`, and run() races each check against it. Outrunning it yields a WARN result, never a fail. |

cli (src/plugins/cli/types.ts):
| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| renderImpl | RenderFn \| undefined | undefined | (line: string) => void render sink for tests; undefined => branded console (@moku-labs/common/cli createBrandConsole). Resolved ONCE in createState. |
| confirmImpl | ConfirmFn \| undefined | undefined | (question: string) => Promise<boolean>; undefined => styled branded confirm (gates cli.clean() without a target — full projectDir wipe). |

env (CORE plugin, seeded in src/config.ts):
| Field | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| providers | [workerSafeProcessEnv()] | core-plugin config is a SHALLOW merge, so passing `providers` REPLACES this list. Re-add workerSafeProcessEnv() or ctx.env.get("PATH") becomes undefined and every build fails with "[native] Could not locate a `node` binary on PATH." The typed createApp pluginConfigs map is keyed by the framework's REGULAR plugins only, so reaching `env` from Layer 3 needs a cast — the kernel merges the key at runtime (cascade level 4).

project and build have NO per-plugin config — they consume global config only.

====================================================================
4. COMPLETE EVENT CATALOG
====================================================================

GLOBAL framework events (declared in src/config.ts Events — D-003). Emitted by build;
hooked by cli; hookable by ANY plugin without a depends edge:

"native:phase" — payload NativePhaseEvent:
  { target: Target;
    phase: "scaffold" | "codegen" | "icons" | "compile" | "bundle" | "collect";
    status: "start" | "progress" | "done" | "error";
    durationMs?: number;   // present on done/error
    detail?: string }      // progress ticks ("Compiling <crate> [i/total]"), icons outcome, error text
  Emission pattern per phase: "start" -> zero or more "progress" (compile only, one per parsed
  crate tick — real cargo counts, never a synthesized percentage) -> "done" | "error".
  After an "error", NO further phase events fire for that run (the pipeline stops).
  compile/bundle share ONE subprocess: the first output line matching /bundling/i closes
  compile and opens bundle WHILE the process is still running. With no such line,
  compile closes at exit and bundle is reported with durationMs 0. A failure is attributed
  to whichever phase is OPEN — a bundling/signing error reads as bundle, not compile.
  The icons phase reports detail "generated", "placeholder" or "up to date".

"native:complete" — payload NativeCompleteEvent:
  { target: Target; outPath: string; artifacts: readonly string[]; durationMs: number }
  Emitted once per successful build.run(), after collect. outPath = outDir/<target>/.

PER-PLUGIN event (declared by doctor via the register callback; hooking requires a
depends: [doctorPlugin] edge for event-type merging):

"doctor:check" — payload CheckResult:
  { id: string;
    target: Target | "host";
    status: "pass" | "warn" | "fail";
    message: string;       // human line, [native]-prefixed
    fixIt?: string }       // actionable next command/step
  Emitted once per check AS IT SETTLES (not batched at the end) — cli renders these live,
  exactly once each, and its summary then prints counts only. Emission order is settle
  order; report.checks keeps registry order.

cli declares NO events — hooks only. Its hook map (handlers.ts):
  "native:phase"    -> updates ctx.state.progress.startedAt and renders a live status line
  "native:complete" -> renders the completion box panel (app name, target, artifact paths, duration)
  "doctor:check"    -> renders the live pass/warn/fail row + fix-it

====================================================================
5. PROJECT PLUGIN (Complex tier — src/plugins/project/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: owns the generated Tauri project as FILES — capability registry,
all generators for projectDir, the write-if-changed content-hash writer, the mobile
completeness gate, the mobile patch pass (Android signing + the runner rewrite), the
placeholder icon, and clean. It NEVER spawns subprocesses. Files: index.ts, types.ts,
api.ts, validate.ts, layout.ts, paths.ts, registry.ts, writer.ts, clean.ts, icon.ts,
mobile/{completeness,signing,runner,patch}.ts,
generators/{tauri-conf,cargo,rust,capabilities,build-script,entitlements,sidecar,paths,types}.ts.

layout.ts is the ONE owner of the generated tree's output layout — the desktop
bundle-FORMAT table, the mobile gen/<platform> directory name and genDirectoryPath().
clean.ts, the completeness gate, the mobile patch pass and (through
project.getBundleLayout) build's collect phase all read it from there; nobody keeps a
second copy.
paths.ts is the ONE owner of path normalization/containment — realpath resolution,
NFC + case rules, and the isDerivedPath() predicate that both the destructive clean
guard and the composition-time config check ask, so what createApp accepts and what
clean() will delete can never drift apart.
mobile/patch.ts is orchestration only: it decides WHICH patches a platform needs and in
which order, while mobile/signing.ts owns the Android Gradle signing block and
mobile/runner.ts owns the Xcode/Android-Studio runner-command rewrite.

Generated artifacts (all through write-if-changed):
| Path (under projectDir) | Generator | Carries |
|---|---|---|
| src-tauri/tauri.conf.json | generators/tauri-conf.ts | identity, web build/dev wiring, bundle metadata, Apple signing, a plugins.<name> block per CONFIGURED capability (empty conf = no key: store/notification/clipboard-manager deserialize `unit` and a `{}` map there aborts startup) |
| src-tauri/Cargo.toml | generators/cargo.ts | package manifest, `tauri = { version = "2", features = [...] }` (sorted unique cargo features), one pinned crate per plugin-backed capability |
| src-tauri/build.rs | generators/build-script.ts | `fn main() { tauri_build::build() }` — without it capabilities are never compiled in and `tauri build` fails |
| src-tauri/src/lib.rs, src/main.rs | generators/rust.ts | mobile entry point + one .plugin(...) line per capability |
| src-tauri/capabilities/default.json | generators/capabilities.ts | "core:default" first, then every capability permission, scoped to Tauri's platform ids (macOS, iOS, windows, linux, android) |
| src-tauri/Entitlements.plist | generators/entitlements.ts | App Store sandbox, only for signing.apple.appStore macOS builds with no consumer plist |
| src-tauri/Info.ios.plist | generators/sidecar.ts | future-mechanism seam — no v1 row emits it |
| placeholder-icon.png | icon.ts | embedded 1024x1024 PNG, written only when app.icon is unset |

Types (src/plugins/project/types.ts — verbatim):

/** Result of a write-if-changed generation pass. */
export type GenerateResult = {
  readonly written: readonly string[];
  readonly unchanged: readonly string[];
  readonly skipped: readonly string[];
};

/** Mobile gen/-tree gate — completeness (required-file set), not existence. */
export type CompletenessResult =
  | { status: "not-applicable" }
  | { status: "not-initialized" }
  | { status: "incomplete"; missing: readonly string[] }
  | { status: "complete" };

/** Result of the idempotent mobile patch pass (Android signing + the mobile runner command). */
export type PatchResult = { readonly patched: readonly string[]; readonly unchanged: readonly string[] };

/** Options for one mobile patch pass. The runner patch is skipped when `runner` is absent. */
export type PatchMobileOptions = {
  target: MobileTarget;
  runner?: TauriRunner | undefined;
};

/** Result of a clean pass. */
export type CleanResult = { removed: readonly string[] };

/**
 * One capability registry row. A row is backed EITHER by a real Tauri plugin (crate + npm
 * package + Rust init) or by a core Tauri cargo feature (tray), so every plugin-only field
 * is optional and `cargoFeatures` is always present.
 */
export type RegistryRow = {
  name: keyof CapabilityConfigMap;
  npmPackage?: `@tauri-apps/plugin-${string}`;
  crate?: `tauri-plugin-${string}`;
  crateRange?: string;
  npmRange?: string;
  rustInit?: string;
  cargoFeatures: readonly string[];
  permissions: readonly string[];
  platforms: readonly Target[];
  confidence: "high" | "medium" | "low";
};

/** The tauri.conf.json plugins["deep-link"] shape — desktop and mobile are separate keys. */
export type DeepLinkConf = {
  desktop: { schemes: readonly string[] };
  mobile: ReadonlyArray<{ scheme: readonly string[]; appLink: boolean }>;
};

/**
 * A tauri.conf.json plugins.<name> contribution — the union of the real v1 shapes. The
 * empty member is the "this plugin takes no config" case: it is never written to
 * tauri.conf.json, because such a plugin deserializes `unit` and a `{}` map there aborts
 * the app at startup.
 */
export type TauriConfFragment = Record<string, never> | DeepLinkConf;

export type PlistEntry = { key: string; value: string };
export type ManifestEntry = { parentTag: string; xml: string };

export type ResolvedCapability = RegistryRow & {
  conf: TauriConfFragment;
  sidecarPlist: readonly PlistEntry[];
  manifest: readonly ManifestEntry[];
};

/** Domain context — core's PluginCtx (no per-plugin config/state/events) + global + log. */
export type ProjectContext = PluginCtx<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>> & {
  readonly global: Readonly<Config>;
  readonly log: LogApi;
};

/** Where one target's build output lives inside the generated project (layout.ts). */
export type BundleFormat = { readonly directory: string; readonly pattern: string };
export type BundleLayout = {
  readonly root: string;                          // relative to projectDir
  readonly formats: readonly BundleFormat[];      // desktop bundle/<format>/ — empty for mobile
  readonly genDirectory: string | undefined;      // gen/<platform> — undefined for desktop
};

/** Absolute gen/<platform> path of a mobile target — the one join every caller uses. */
export function genDirectoryPath(projectDirectory: string, target: MobileTarget): string;

/** Public API of the project plugin. */
export type Api = {
  generate(opts: { target: Target }): Promise<GenerateResult>;
  getBundleLayout(opts: { target: Target }): BundleLayout;
  getCompleteness(opts: { target: Target }): CompletenessResult;
  patchMobile(opts: PatchMobileOptions): Promise<PatchResult>;
  clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<CleanResult>;
  clearMobileBuildOutput(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): Promise<CleanResult>;
  ensureIconSource(): Promise<string>;
  resolve<K extends keyof CapabilityConfigMap>(
    name: K,
    config?: CapabilityConfigMap[K]
  ): ResolvedCapability;
  isKnownCapability(name: string): name is keyof CapabilityConfigMap;
  getRegistryRows(): ReadonlyArray<RegistryRow>;
  getRequiredFiles(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): readonly string[];
};

Generator input types (src/plugins/project/generators/types.ts — verbatim):

export type GeneratorInput = {
  global: Readonly<Config>;
  target: Target;
  capabilities: readonly ResolvedCapability[]; // resolved from config.system, platform-filtered
};

export type Artifact = {
  path: string;    // relative to projectDir, e.g. "src-tauri/tauri.conf.json"
  content: string;
};

Behavior:
- generate({ target }): resolves config.system against the registry (unknown names throw),
  filters rows to those whose platforms include the target, runs the generators, writes each
  artifact via write-if-changed under projectDir. Desktop targets get the whole tree; mobile
  targets get the shared tree + conf (the gen/ tree itself is created by `tauri ios|android
  init`, never by this plugin). Path-shaped conf fields (build.frontendDist,
  bundle.macOS.entitlements) are rebased onto src-tauri in POSIX form, because that is where
  Tauri resolves them from; beforeDevCommand/beforeBuildCommand use the OBJECT form with
  an explicit cwd = path.resolve(web.cwd ?? ".").
- getCompleteness({ target }): mobile gen/<platform> required-file-set gate. Desktop => "not-applicable".
- getBundleLayout({ target }): the target's output root, its desktop bundle-format directories
  with their artifact globs, and its mobile gen/<platform> directory — straight from layout.ts.
  build's collect phase globs against this instead of keeping its own table.
- patchMobile({ target, runner? }): idempotent post-init patch.
    * iOS: rewrites the runner command in gen/apple/project.yml (YAML scalar quoting) and in
      every gen/apple/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj (escaped \" quoting, because the value sits
      inside a pbxproj string). The match is runner-AGNOSTIC but NARROW: on any line carrying
      " ios xcode-script", only the runner-shaped token run DIRECTLY before the verb is
      replaced, so `node tauri`, `bun tauri`, `npm run tauri --`, `yarn|pnpm tauri`,
      `cargo tauri`, a bare `tauri` and an already-absolute pair all normalize to
      `"<node>" "<tauri.js>"` while everything else on the line (a `set -e` / `cd "$SRCROOT" &&`
      preamble, the verb's own arguments) survives byte for byte. Each path is escaped for the
      double-quoted shell word it lands in (\, ", $, backtick) and a path containing a line
      break is refused with a [native] error. Omit `runner` and the rewrite is skipped. A second
      pass reports every file unchanged — but an absolute pair whose node path CHANGED (an
      fnm/nvm switch) is re-patched, not left stale. A file that carries the verb behind a
      runner shape the match does NOT recognize throws
      '[native] Could not find a Tauri runner command before "<verb>" in <file>.\n  Set
      pluginConfigs.tauri.nodePath, or report the runner line Tauri generated.' rather than
      being reported unchanged — reporting success there ships a tree that fails on its first
      build phase. A file that never mentions the verb stays unchanged.
      iOS ALSO gets the rebuild patch, with or without a `runner`: every `buildSettings = {`
      block of each gen/apple/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj carries
      `CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION = YES;` exactly once, at its siblings'
      indentation, and each target's settings.base in gen/apple/project.yml carries
      `CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION: true` (so an xcodegen regeneration keeps
      it; a settingGroups base block is never touched). Without it the SECOND build of a tree
      fails: a capability plugin's build script rewrites <app>_iOS.entitlements mid-build and
      Xcode refuses ("Entitlements file … was modified during the build"). Both transforms are
      pure text — CRLF, indentation and neighbouring lines survive byte for byte, a block that
      already carries the setting is left alone, a block that set it to NO is rewritten to YES,
      and a second pass reports every file unchanged. A file touched by both iOS patches is
      reported once, as patched.
    * Android: the same rewrite for " android android-studio-script" across
      gen/android/buildSrc/**/*.{kt,kts,gradle} and the two top-level build.gradle.kts, PLUS a
      sentinel-delimited `// MOKU-SIGNING-START … // MOKU-SIGNING-END` block in
      gen/android/app/build.gradle.kts (signingConfigs.maybeCreate("release") with storeFile,
      keyAlias, storePassword/keyPassword read via System.getenv, and
      buildTypes.getByName("release").signingConfig). Every interpolated value (keystore path,
      key alias, env-var names) goes through kotlinString() first — \, ", $ and newlines are
      escaped — so a value can neither close the literal nor interpolate a Gradle expression.
      No keystore.properties is written any
      more; an unset keystorePath REMOVES the block and deletes a legacy keystore.properties
      (a single named file inside gen/android, never a recursive remove).
- ensureIconSource(): app.icon set => path.resolve(app.icon), throwing a [native] fix-it when
  the file is missing. Unset => writes the embedded 1024x1024 placeholder PNG to
  <projectDir>/placeholder-icon.png via write-if-changed and returns that path.
- clean({ target? }): mobile target => gen/<platform> only; desktop target => that target's
  bundle output; omitted => the whole projectDir. `assertCleanableRoot(root, cwd, home,
  platform)` runs FIRST, on the positive-containment rule from paths.ts: projectDir must
  resolve (realpath, NFC + case-insensitive on darwin/win32) strictly INSIDE the PROJECT
  ANCHOR or a usable OS temp root, and must not be — or contain — the anchor, the cwd or the
  home directory, nor be a filesystem root. "~/Documents" is refused for the same reason "/"
  is: it is not derived state. Every surviving candidate path is validated against projectDir
  by assertWithinRoot before deletion.
- clearMobileBuildOutput({ target }): removes the PREVIOUS build output of a mobile target so
  the next compile writes into an empty tree — ios => <projectDir>/src-tauri/gen/apple/build
  (the path comes from layout.ts), android => nothing removed at all, because Gradle owns and
  correctly reuses its own build tree. Without it the SECOND `tauri ios build` of a tree dies
  with 'failed to rename app …/gen/apple/build/<app>_iOS.xcarchive/…/<Name>.app: Directory not
  empty (os error 66)'. A missing directory is fine ({ removed: [] }). Being a second
  recursive delete, it is gated twice: assertCleanableRoot(projectDir) — the same derived-path
  rule clean() uses — and the pure predicate isClearableBuildOutput(root, candidate,
  boundaries), which requires the REAL path of the build directory (symlinks resolved) to sit
  STRICTLY inside the real projectDir. A `build` symlink pointing elsewhere is refused, never
  followed: '[native] Refusing to remove build output outside projectDir: <real path>.\n
  Remove that link by hand — "<path>" must be a real directory inside <projectDir>.' The
  predicate is pure and is tested as one; the destructive function is only ever run against a
  fresh mkdtemp workspace.
  containmentAnchor(cwd, home, platform, probe): the nearest ancestor of the cwd (cwd
  included) carrying a .git entry or a package.json with a "workspaces" field, walking up but
  stopping BEFORE $HOME and before a filesystem root; no marker anywhere => the cwd stands.
  Measuring against the cwd alone broke a monorepo whose absolute projectDir sits at the
  repository root while the script runs from packages/app. Pure function over an injectable
  AnchorProbe { hasEntry, readText }.
  A temp root that IS a filesystem root, or that is/contains $HOME, grants nothing —
  os.tmpdir() follows TMPDIR, so TMPDIR=/ would otherwise bless the whole disk.
- resolveDerivedPath(path): the ONE comparable form every containment guard compares in —
  realResolve (symlinks followed) + NFC + case folding on darwin/win32. Comparison only,
  never for display or a filesystem call. build's collect guard consumes it through
  BuildDeps instead of keeping a second, lexical copy.
- resolve(name, config?): typed registry lookup; throws when name isn't in the registry, or
  when resolving "deep-link" without a non-empty scheme.
- getRegistryRows(): fresh COPIES — a caller can never mutate the registry.
- onInit: validateProjectConfig(ctx.global) from validate.ts — see section 12.

Writer safety: assertWritablePath refuses (a) any path OUTSIDE projectDir — an empty,
".."-leading or absolute relative form — with '[native] Refusing to write outside
projectDir: <path>.', and (b) writes into target/, .gradle/, DerivedData or Pods,
scanning ONLY the path BELOW projectDir — a repository checked out under a directory
called "target" is a normal checkout, not a violation.

Capability registry rows (registry.ts):
| name | backing | platforms | permissions | confidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| store | crate + @tauri-apps/plugin-store + rust init | all five | store:default | high |
| notification | crate + @tauri-apps/plugin-notification + rust init | all five | notification:default | high |
| clipboard-manager | crate + @tauri-apps/plugin-clipboard-manager + rust init | all five | clipboard-manager:allow-read-text, clipboard-manager:allow-write-text | high |
| tray | CARGO FEATURE "tray-icon" only — no crate, no npm package, no rust init | macos, windows, linux | core:tray:default, core:menu:default, core:image:default, core:resources:default, core:app:allow-default-window-icon | low |
| deep-link | crate + @tauri-apps/plugin-deep-link + rust init | all five (custom-scheme-only, D-011) | deep-link:default | high |

tray lists five permissions on purpose. @moku-labs/system defaults the tray icon to
defaultWindowIcon() from @tauri-apps/api/app, and core:default does NOT grant that command:
a real macOS shell fails at startup with
  Command plugin:app|default_window_icon not allowed by ACL
core:app:allow-default-window-icon is the grant. The menu, image and resources ids are
already covered by core:default and are spelled out anyway, so the row documents every
core surface tray actually touches instead of leaning on the baseline set.

deep-link resolves to the plugin's real two-sided conf shape:
  { "desktop": { "schemes": ["myapp"] },
    "mobile": [{ "scheme": ["myapp"], "appLink": false }] }

v1 mobile permission codegen is conf-only (D-012): every registry row's sidecarPlist and
manifest arrays are EMPTY — official Tauri plugins self-merge their own AndroidManifest needs
via build.rs, and deep-link's iOS CFBundleURLTypes ride Tauri's own sidecar merge.

====================================================================
6. TAURI PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/tauri/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the framework's ONLY @tauri-apps/cli subprocess seam — argv builders,
injectable spawn, process-group dev lifecycle, stream parsing, error taxonomy, secret
scrubbing. Invocation shape (D-013): [nodePath, tauriJsPath, verb, ...args] — explicit
PATH-walked real node binary against require.resolve("@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js").
Never `bunx tauri`, never --bun runtime, never the platform .node addon directly.
Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, argv.ts, resolve.ts, spawn.ts, dev.ts, stream.ts,
errors.ts, scrub.ts, state.ts.

Types (src/plugins/tauri/types.ts — verbatim):

/** Structural spawn seam — injectable for tests. */
export type SpawnFn = (opts: {
  cmd: readonly string[];
  cwd: string;
  env?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
  detached?: boolean;
  onLine?: (line: string) => void;
  signal?: AbortSignal;
}) => Promise<{ code: number | null; signal: string | null; stdout: string; stderr: string }>;

/** tauri plugin per-plugin config — test seams. */
export type Config = {
  spawnImpl?: SpawnFn | undefined;
  nodePath?: string | undefined;
  arch?: NodeJS.Architecture | undefined;
  readiness: { intervalMs: number; timeoutMs: number };
};

/** Result of a one-shot verb (non-zero exits throw TauriError instead). */
export type RunResult = { code: 0; stdout: string; stderr: string; durationMs: number };

/** Parsed compile progress tick — real crate counts, never fake percentages. */
export type CompileTick = { crate: string; index?: number; total?: number };

/** The build verb's full option surface — everything that changes the argv. */
export type BuildArgvOptions = BuildFlavor & {
  target: Target;
  simulator?: boolean | undefined;      // iOS only
  exportMethod?: AppleExportMethod | undefined;  // iOS device builds only
  aab?: boolean | undefined;            // Android only
};

export type BuildOptions = BuildArgvOptions & {
  onTick?: (tick: CompileTick) => void;
  onOutput?: (line: string) => void;
};

/** How a dev session ended. */
export type DevExit = { code: number | null; signal: string | null };

/** Live dev-session handle — teardown is owned HERE (D-002), never by cli. */
export type DevHandle = {
  url: string;
  ready: Promise<void>;
  exited: Promise<DevExit>;
  stop(): Promise<void>;
};

/** Classified subprocess failure taxonomy. */
export type TauriErrorKind =
  | "toolchain-missing"
  | "platform-missing"
  | "config-invalid"
  | "compile-failed"
  | "xcode-script-failed"
  | "signing-failed"
  | "device-unavailable"
  | "cancelled"
  | "unknown";

export type TauriErrorDetails = {
  readonly kind: TauriErrorKind;
  readonly exitCode: number | null;   // null when signal-terminated
  readonly stderrTail: string;        // scrubbed — safe to log/display
};

/** Thrown by every one-shot verb (icon/build/mobileInit) on a non-zero exit. Lives in errors.ts. */
export class TauriError extends Error implements TauriErrorDetails { ... }

/** Mutable plugin state — the one live dev handle (undefined = no live session). */
export type State = { dev: DevHandle | undefined };

/** Public API of the tauri plugin — the framework's ONLY subprocess seam. */
export type Api = {
  icon(opts: { source: string }): Promise<RunResult>;
  build(opts: BuildOptions): Promise<RunResult>;
  mobileInit(opts: { target: MobileTarget }): Promise<RunResult>;
  dev(opts: { target?: Target; onOutput?: (line: string) => void }): Promise<DevHandle>;
  getVersion(): Promise<{ cliVersion: string } | undefined>;
  getRunner(): TauriRunner;
};

Behavior:
- icon({ source }): runs `tauri icon <source> --output <absolute projectDir>/src-tauri/icons`.
  Without the explicit --output the CLI writes relative to its own cwd, which is not the
  generated project. Called by build's icons phase.
- build(opts): runs `tauri build` / `tauri ios build` / `tauri android build`, always with
  --ci. argv rules (buildArgv): ios + simulator => `--target aarch64-sim` (`x86_64`, no -sim
  suffix, on an x64 host; the arch comes from config.arch, defaulting to process.arch, so a
  test can pin it) and NO --export-method; ios without simulator => `--export-method <m>` when
  configured; android => `--aab` when aab, else `--apk`; desktop unchanged. An option a target
  does not use is ignored, never an error. Every output line is scrubbed before reaching
  onOutput or a log; onTick receives parsed compile progress. Throws a classified TauriError
  on a non-zero exit, classified from BOTH scrubbed streams (xcodebuild writes the cause to
  stdout).
- mobileInit({ target }): runs `tauri ios|android init --ci` — the ONLY init verbs exposed
  (plain `tauri init` is never used; the desktop tree is project-generated). NOT idempotent
  (tauri#13902) — callers gate on project.getCompleteness() === "not-initialized" first. It also
  requires tauri.conf.json to exist already, which is why codegen (not scaffold) runs it.
- getRunner(): the resolved { nodePath, tauriJsPath } pair every verb spawns with — fed to
  project.patchMobile so the Xcode/Android build phase invokes the very same CLI.
- dev({ target?, onOutput? }): starts the long-lived dev verb in a detached process group,
  installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers (group-kill + handler removal on exit), returns a DevHandle
  immediately. `ready` resolves from a devUrl readiness poll (config.readiness, each probe
  bounded by a 2s fetch timeout; no stdout
  "ready" marker exists — tauri#4740) and rejects (reaping the process group) on timeout, or
  as soon as the session is over: "[native] dev session stopped before the dev server became
  ready." when stop() was called or the dev process exited first.
  A second concurrent dev() call throws "[native] tauri dev already running". stop() never
  rejects. url = ctx.global.web.devUrl.
- getVersion(): probes CLI presence/version via `tauri info` (used by doctor). Returns undefined
  when the CLI cannot be invoked — never throws.

cwd: one-shot verbs run in projectDir once it EXISTS, else in the consumer's cwd —
icon/version legitimately run before scaffold created it, and spawning into a missing
directory fails with a bare ENOENT instead of a [native] message. dev always uses projectDir.

spawn.ts: a run resolves when the child's stdio pipes CLOSE, not when the process
exits — tauri's own children (xcodebuild, gradle, cargo) inherit those pipes and keep writing
after the parent is gone, and resolving on `exit` drops exactly the tail an error is made of.
The group-kill ladder still watches `exit`. The one `process.env` read lives in a single
function `inheritedEnvironment`, with the MC3 exception stated inline: a child process needs
the full parent environment, while ctx.env exposes declared keys only.
killProcessGroup signals the NEGATED pid only when this spawn created the group
(`detached: true` — dev); a one-shot verb spawns attached and shares the parent's group, so
it is signalled by plain pid. Both signals are best-effort (try/catch: an ESRCH from a
process that exited a microsecond earlier must not become an unhandled rejection inside an
abort handler), and the SIGKILL rung waits a 250ms settle window for the exit instead of
claiming the process is gone the instant the signal is sent.

Secret scrubbing (scrub.ts): four passes, in order.
  1. known secret env-var names (APPLE_PASSWORD, APPLE_CERTIFICATE*, APPLE_API_KEY*,
     TAURI_SIGNING_*, ANDROID_KEY*_PASSWORD) — ALWAYS masked, whatever the entropy. The
     value capture is `"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|\S+`, so a quoted password with spaces does not
     leak its tail.
  2. URL userinfo: scheme://user:token@host => scheme://[native:scrubbed]@host, always —
     a URL is location-shaped and would otherwise be exempt.
  3. long hex runs: a standalone run of >= 32 hex chars (digests, keys). Hex tops out at
     EXACTLY 4.0 bits/char, so the entropy pass can never reach it. A git sha announced by
     "commit ", "rev " or a leading "#" stays readable.
  4. Shannon entropy: any remaining token of length >= 20 at or above 4.0 bits/char.
A location-shaped token (one carrying "/", "\" or "::") is NOT exempt from the entropy
pass — it is scanned PART by PART, where a part is the run between two "-", "." or "#"
delimiters, so /var/tmp/<secret>/App.dmg loses only the secret while a build name glued to a
hash stays readable: libtauri_app-<hash>.rlib, moku-native-app-<hash>.dSYM, Xcode's
DerivedData/<name>-<hash>/, a content-hashed main-<hash>.css. Judging whole segments masked
all four. Kept readable by name: canonical 8-4-4-4-12 UUIDs with an optional short key:
prefix/punctuation (simulator destination lists), the cargo registry's
index.crates.io-<hash> segment, and a published digest announced by its context — "commit ",
"rev ", a cargo git+<url># source fragment, or Cargo.lock's `checksum = "`. A BARE "#" is
not a context: it prefixes anchors, issue numbers and shell comments. No output path
bypasses the scrubber.

====================================================================
7. BUILD PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/build/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the per-target packaging orchestrator. Runs scaffold -> codegen -> icons ->
compile -> bundle -> collect for one target, delegating scaffold/codegen to project and
icons/compile/bundle to tauri — build never spawns a process itself. Owns exactly one phase
directly: collect. depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin]. No config, no state, no onInit.
Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, pipeline.ts, collect.ts (no bundle table of its own — the
layout arrives through deps from project.getBundleLayout).

Types (src/plugins/build/types.ts — verbatim):

export type PhaseTiming = { phase: NativePhase; durationMs: number };

/** Result of one target's full pipeline pass — `phases` always carries all six entries. */
export type BuildResult = {
  target: Target;
  outPath: string;
  artifacts: readonly string[];
  durationMs: number;
  phases: readonly PhaseTiming[];
};

export type RunOptions = {
  target: Target;
  simulator?: boolean | undefined;   // iOS
  aab?: boolean | undefined;         // Android
};

export type RunAllOptions = {
  targets?: readonly Target[] | undefined;
  simulator?: boolean | undefined;
  aab?: boolean | undefined;
};

/** The dependency API slices the pipeline calls, resolved ONCE in createBuildApi. */
export type BuildDeps = {
  readonly project: Pick<
    ProjectApi,
    | "generate"
    | "getBundleLayout"
    | "getCompleteness"
    | "patchMobile"
    | "clearMobileBuildOutput"
    | "ensureIconSource"
    | "resolveDerivedPath"
  >;
  readonly tauri: Pick<TauriApi, "build" | "mobileInit" | "icon" | "getRunner">;
};

/** Public API of the build plugin — the per-target pipeline orchestrator. */
export type Api = {
  prepare(opts: { target: Target }): Promise<void>;
  run(opts: RunOptions): Promise<BuildResult>;
  runAll(opts?: RunAllOptions): Promise<readonly BuildResult[]>;
};

/** Domain context: core's PluginCtx + global + log + a require constrained to the deps. */
export type BuildContext = PluginCtx<Record<string, never>, Record<string, never>, Events> & {
  readonly global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>;
  readonly log: LogApi;
  require<P extends typeof projectPlugin | typeof tauriPlugin>(plugin: P): P["_phantom"]["api"];
};

Phase semantics (pipeline.ts):
| Phase | Delegate | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| scaffold | own | mkdir -p projectDir. Nothing else: the mobile gen/ tree is initialized in codegen, because `tauri ios\|android init --ci` refuses to run before tauri.conf.json exists. |
| codegen | project + tauri | project.generate() first. Mobile then: tauri.mobileInit({ target }) when project.getCompleteness() is "not-initialized", the completeness gate ("incomplete" FAILS FAST with a [native] fix-it pointing at `native doctor` / `native clean --target <t>` — a partial tree is never silently re-initialized), then the idempotent project.patchMobile({ target, runner: tauri.getRunner() }). |
| icons | project + tauri | source = await project.ensureIconSource(); regeneration is skipped ONLY when src-tauri/icons/icon.png exists, the stamp file src-tauri/icons/.source (absolute source path + size + mtime) still matches the current source, AND this pass did not run mobileInit (a fresh gen/ tree ships Tauri's default icons) — an mtime comparison alone would miss app.icon switching to an OLDER file. Else tauri.icon({ source }). detail: "up to date" / "generated" / "placeholder". |
| compile | project + tauri.build() | ios FIRST: project.clearMobileBuildOutput({ target }) removes gen/apple/build (a second `tauri ios build` otherwise fails renaming its .app into the previous archive). It runs INSIDE the compile phase, so a refusal is a compile error and tauri.build never starts; something removed => one compile `progress` event with detail "cleared previous build output", nothing removed => silence. Desktop/android skip it. Then ONE subprocess covers compile+bundle. compile carries the live onTick progress stream. |
| bundle | (same subprocess) | LIVE transition on the first /bundling/i output line; zero-duration fallback when absent; a failure is attributed to the OPEN phase. |
| collect | own (collect.ts) | Locates artifacts via the layout from project.getBundleLayout({ target }), copies to outDir/<target>/, REMOVING each destination first (fs.cp merges into an existing .app and would keep stale files inside the bundle) after asserting — on REAL paths, through project.resolveDerivedPath threaded in as CollectInput.resolvePath — that the destination is strictly inside <outDir>/<target> and that directory strictly inside outDir; a lexical guard reads a symlinked <outDir>/<target> as contained and the next statement deletes the tree it points at. Matches are deduplicated by destination name, keeping the NEWEST by mtime (a mobile build leaves one directory per arch and never prunes the ones it did not rebuild, so "whichever the glob yielded last" could ship yesterday's binary). ZERO matches is an error — never a silent empty success. |

prepare({ target }) runs scaffold -> codegen -> icons and stops: everything that makes the
generated project buildable, without invoking the build verb. cli.dev calls it first.

collect.ts keeps NO bundle table of its own. The layout comes from project (layout.ts) through
deps as a BundleLayout; bundleRoot(projectDir, layout) resolves the root and
bundlePatterns(layout, target, opts) turns it into globs:
  macos:   ["bundle/dmg/*.dmg", "bundle/macos/*.app"]        (root: src-tauri/target/release/)
  windows: ["bundle/nsis/*-setup.exe", "bundle/msi/*.msi"]   (root: src-tauri/target/release/)
  linux:   ["bundle/appimage/*.AppImage", "bundle/deb/*.deb", "bundle/rpm/*.rpm"]
  ios:     ["gen/apple/build/**/*.ipa"]                      (root: src-tauri/)
  android: ["gen/android/app/build/outputs/apk/**/*elease*/*.apk"] (root: src-tauri/)
One flavour at a time, never two: { simulator: true } matches
["gen/apple/build/*-sim/*.app", "gen/apple/build/x86_64/*.app"] — both directory names Tauri
can write a simulator slice under — INSTEAD of the .ipa (a simulator build is unsigned and produces a .app DIRECTORY whose name
carries the display name, spaces included), and { aab: true } matches
["gen/android/app/build/outputs/bundle/**/*elease*/*.aab"] INSTEAD of the .apk. The release
flavour is pinned in the glob: Gradle writes every build type side by side, so an unpinned
outputs/** pattern ships a debug installer. Copies use
fs.cp(..., { recursive: true }) so a .app bundle and single-file installers share one call.

runAll({ targets?, simulator?, aab? }): sequential for every target (default
ctx.global.targets) — NEVER Promise.all: all targets share one Cargo target/ lock, so
parallelism would only contend. Stops at the first failing target.

====================================================================
8. DOCTOR PLUGIN (Complex tier — src/plugins/doctor/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: diagnoses whether a target is actually buildable — toolchain presence, mobile
gen/-tree completeness, npm-vs-crate version skew, signing readiness, and warn-only cross-repo
pointers. depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin]. Declares and emits doctor:check. Files:
index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, report.ts, checks/ (13 check modules + registry + shared types).

Types (src/plugins/doctor/types.ts — verbatim):

export type ProbeFn = (
  cmd: string,
  args: readonly string[]
) => Promise<{ code: number; stdout: string }>;

export type Config = {
  probeImpl?: ProbeFn | undefined;
  probeTimeoutMs: number;    // default 10_000
};

export type CheckResult = {
  id: string;
  target: Target | "host";
  status: "pass" | "warn" | "fail";
  message: string;
  fixIt?: string;
};

export type DoctorReport = { ok: boolean; checks: readonly CheckResult[] };

export type DoctorEvents = { "doctor:check": CheckResult };

export type Api = {
  run(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<DoctorReport>;
};

Check interface (src/plugins/doctor/checks/types.ts — the providers pattern):

export type FsFacade = { readFile(path: string): Promise<string> };
export type CheckProjectApi = Pick<ProjectApi, "getRequiredFiles" | "getCompleteness" | "getRegistryRows">;
export type CheckTauriApi = Pick<TauriApi, "version">;

export type CheckInput = {
  target: Target | "host";
  global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>;
  probe: ProbeFn;      // doctor's own seam — never tauri's
  fs: FsFacade;
  env: EnvApi;         // presence only for signing (env.has, never env.get into messages)
  project: CheckProjectApi;
  tauri: CheckTauriApi;
};

export type Check = {
  id: string;
  appliesTo(target: Target | "host", global: Readonly<GlobalConfig>): boolean;
  run(input: CheckInput): Promise<CheckResult>;
};

The checks/ registry (CHECKS order: node, tauri-cli, rustup, xcode, ios-tools, ios-platform,
android, signing, completeness, versions, web-script, cross-repo-cors, cross-repo-deep-link):
| Module | Diagnoses | Posture |
|---|---|---|
| node.ts | a real node binary on PATH, distinct from bun (tauri#9939) | fail |
| tauri-cli.ts | CLI invokable via tauri.getVersion() — the one probe routed through tauri | fail |
| rustup.ts | rustup present; the target's required rust triple installed | fail |
| xcode.ts | Xcode/xcodebuild present, simulators queryable (ios, macOS host only) | fail |
| ios-tools.ts | xcodegen + pod on PATH and both rust triples (aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim) installed via `rustup target list --installed` (ios, macOS host only). fixIt lists the exact install commands (brew install xcodegen; brew install cocoapods; rustup target add …) | fail |
| ios-platform.ts | the installed iOS platform: `xcodebuild -showsdks` + `xcrun simctl list runtimes` (ios, macOS host only). Warns ONLY when no simulator runtime is installed — a runtime newer than the SDK is fine. fixIt: `xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS` | warn only |
| android.ts | ANDROID_HOME/SDK, NDK, JDK presence (android) | fail |
| signing.ts | Apple: one COMPLETE credential set (APPLE_ID+APPLE_PASSWORD+APPLE_TEAM_ID, or APPLE_API_KEY+APPLE_API_ISSUER+APPLE_API_KEY_PATH); ios additionally wants signing.apple.teamId; a COUNT-only keychain probe (`security find-identity -v -p codesigning`) skipped when signingIdentity is unset or "-" or when APPLE_CERTIFICATE is set. Android: presence of signing.android.keystorePasswordEnv. Every message says unsigned and simulator builds are legal | warn only |
| completeness.ts | mobile gen/ required-file-set via project.getCompleteness(); fixIt is always `native clean --target <t>` | fail (not-initialized = pass) |
| versions.ts | @tauri-apps/* npm major version vs. the registry-pinned crate range, read from path.resolve(web.cwd ?? "."); rows without an npmPackage (tray) are skipped | warn only |
| web-script.ts | web.build/web.devCommand scripts exist in the SAME root Tauri will use (web.cwd when set, else the consumer root); never executes the script | fail |
| cross-repo.ts | worker CORS must allow tauri://localhost / http://tauri.localhost (always fires); deep-link .well-known pointer (only when deep-link is composed) | warn only, always |

Behavior (api.ts):
- run({ target }) => every check whose appliesTo(target, global) is true, for that one scope.
- run() => every check for each of config.targets, PLUS every host-scoped check once
  (scopes = [...ctx.global.targets, "host"]).
- All scheduled (check, scope) pairs run in parallel via Promise.allSettled. Each is RACED
  against config.probeTimeoutMs; a timeout yields
  `[native] doctor check "<id>" timed out.` as a WARN under the id the check itself would
  have produced (Check.resultId(scope), e.g. "signing-macos"), with a fix-it to re-run or raise
  pluginConfigs.doctor.probeTimeoutMs. The real probe additionally passes { timeout } to spawn.
- A rejected check becomes an internal-error "fail" CheckResult (report.ts) — one broken check
  can never sink the report; run() itself only throws on an orchestration bug.
- Each result is emitted as doctor:check AS IT SETTLES, then aggregated: ok === no "fail" rows.

====================================================================
9. CLI PLUGIN (Standard tier — src/plugins/cli/)
====================================================================

Responsibility: the consumer-facing verb layer — typed API methods, NO argv parsing.
Every output line flows through the branded kit @moku-labs/common/cli (MC1:
createBrandConsole, box, spinnerFrameAt, styled confirm) — never raw console.*
(test-enforced via spy). depends: [projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin].
Files: index.ts, types.ts, api.ts, handlers.ts, render.ts, state.ts.

Types (src/plugins/cli/types.ts — verbatim):

export type RenderFn = (line: string) => void;
export type ConfirmFn = (question: string) => Promise<boolean>;

export type Config = {
  renderImpl?: RenderFn | undefined;
  confirmImpl?: ConfirmFn | undefined;
};

/** The ONE branded console (built once in createState) plus live-render bookkeeping. */
export type State = {
  readonly ui: BrandConsole;
  progress: { startedAt: number | undefined };
};

/** Public API of the cli plugin — typed verbs, NO argv parsing. */
export type Api = {
  build(opts?: {
    target?: Target;
    all?: boolean;
    simulator?: boolean | undefined;
    aab?: boolean | undefined;
  }): Promise<void>;
  dev(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;
  doctor(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<boolean>;
  clean(opts?: { target?: Target }): Promise<void>;
};

Behavior (api.ts):
- build(opts?): one target (default: hostTarget() — darwin->macos, win32->windows,
  linux->linux via the framework's own hostTargets; mobile is NEVER inferred; an unknown host
  platform throws a [native] error) or every configured target with { all: true } (ignores
  target). simulator/aab pass straight through to build.run/build.runAll. On failure the
  classified TauriError's scrubbed stderrTail is framed in a branded box ABOVE the [native]
  error line — then the error rethrows unchanged. How wide a tail line may be is the pure
  decision tailLineBound(columns): a stream WITH columns gets max(40, terminalWidth(columns)
  - 6) — the clamped terminal width minus the box chrome, so the whole box fits the terminal
  the kit aligns to (a fixed 160 wrapped every 80-column terminal) — and a stream with NO
  columns (CI, `native build > build.log`, any pipe) gets no bound at all: nothing wraps
  against a file, and truncating there would delete the only copy of the toolchain's own
  error text. renderBuildFailure(ui, error, columns = process.stdout.columns) takes the
  column count as an argument, so tests never depend on the terminal they run in.
- dev(opts?): awaits build.prepare({ target }) FIRST, so `tauri dev` never meets a
  half-generated tree; then tauri.dev(...) and the handle's `ready` then `exited`, forwarding
  scrubbed output lines to the render seam. It NEVER stores the handle and NEVER calls stop()
  (D-002). A signal-terminated exit (code: null — Ctrl-C) is the NORMAL stop and resolves
  cleanly; only a numeric non-zero code throws "[native] tauri dev exited with code N".
- doctor(opts?): delegates to doctor.run. Each check's row (with fix-it) prints exactly ONCE,
  live from the doctor:check hook as it settles; this verb adds only the
  `pass N · warn N · fail N` counts and the verdict. Returns report.ok — the CONSUMER
  SCRIPT sets process.exitCode.
- clean(opts?): thin delegate to project.clean (D-006). Without a target, the full projectDir
  wipe is gated behind a styled confirm; declining resolves without deleting anything.

hostTarget signature (exported from cli/api.ts, not the package root):
  function hostTarget(platform: NodeJS.Platform = process.platform): Target

Hooks (handlers.ts): "native:phase", "native:complete", "doctor:check" — see section 4. The
running phase's startedAt lives in ctx.state.progress, not in closure variables.

Lifecycle (index.ts): onInit runs `ctx.log.clearSinks()` then
`ctx.log.addSink(createLogSink(ctx.state.ui))` — composing cli hands the framework's log
output to the branded console, so a ctx.log record prints as `› event {"data":…}` (payload
dim) instead of a raw { level, event, data, ts } object between the branded lines. Threshold
is "info": debug records (the raw `tauri info` dump doctor keeps) stay in the in-memory trace.
The sink takes the console rather than building its own, which is what keeps the renderImpl
seam whole — with a seam injected, log lines are captured with every other line and a composed
app makes zero raw console.* calls. No onStart, no onStop (D-002).

====================================================================
10. PUBLIC EXPORTS (src/index.ts + src/plugins/index.ts)
====================================================================

import {
  // Framework API
  createApp,     // Layer-3 factory: createApp({ config?, plugins?, pluginConfigs? })
  createPlugin,  // consumer-plugin factory bound to this framework's Config/Events chain
  // Plugin instances
  projectPlugin, tauriPlugin, buildPlugin, doctorPlugin, cliPlugin,
  // Helpers + constants
  hostTargets, PHASE_ORDER, TARGETS,
  // The ONE runtime value a type-only namespace cannot carry
  TauriError,
  // Shared types
  type AppleExportMethod, type AppleSigning, type CapabilityConfigMap, type Config,
  type BuildFlavor, type Events, type MobileTarget, type NativeCompleteEvent,
  type NativePhase, type NativePhaseEvent, type SigningConfig, type Target, type TauriRunner,
  // Per-plugin TYPE-ONLY namespaces (`export type * as X`) — each is the plugin's types module
  type Project, type Tauri, type Build, type Doctor, type Cli
  //   e.g. Project.Api, Project.RegistryRow, Project.PatchResult, Tauri.DevHandle,
  //        Tauri.SpawnFn, Build.BuildResult, Doctor.DoctorReport, Doctor.CheckResult, Cli.RenderFn
} from "@moku-labs/native";

Section order in src/index.ts: Framework API -> Plugins -> Helpers + Constants -> Types.
The file's JSDoc carries the global-config defaults table and the pluginConfigs defaults
table; there is NO pluginConfigs block in the createCore call.

Because the namespaces are type-only, `instanceof TauriError` needs the named import above —
`Tauri.TauriError` is a type, not a value.

====================================================================
11. USAGE EXAMPLES
====================================================================

--- The two-createApp consumer composition (D-009) ---

// src/system.ts — the shared system-plugin composition: the cross-team contract.
export const systemPlugins = [
  { name: "store" },
  { name: "notification" },
  { name: "deep-link" }
];

// src/native.ts — the native createApp (Layer 3), beside your web app entry
import { createApp } from "@moku-labs/native";
import { systemPlugins } from "./system";

export const native = createApp({
  config: {
    app: {
      name: "MyApp",
      identifier: "com.example.myapp",
      icon: "assets/icon.png",      // 1024x1024 PNG; omit for a generated placeholder
      category: "public.app-category.productivity",
      buildNumber: "42"
    },
    web: {
      build: "bun run build",
      devCommand: "bun run dev", devUrl: "http://localhost:5173",
      dist: "dist"
      // cwd: "packages/web"       // monorepo: everything web-shaped resolves from here
    },
    system: systemPlugins,
    capabilities: { "deep-link": { mode: "scheme", scheme: "myapp" } },
    targets: ["macos", "ios"],     // default: hostTargets(process.platform) — mobile is opt-in
    signing: {
      apple: { teamId: "ABCDE12345", exportMethod: "app-store-connect", appStore: true }
    }
  }
});

// package.json — thin per-verb consumer scripts (no argv CLI exists)
// { "scripts": { "native:dev": "bun run scripts/native-dev.ts", ... } }

// scripts/native-build.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.build({ target: "macos" });               // installers -> dist-native/macos/
await native.cli.build({ target: "ios", simulator: true }); // unsigned .app -> dist-native/ios/
await native.stop();

// scripts/native-dev.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.dev();          // prepares, then runs until the session exits (Ctrl-C is clean)
await native.stop();

// scripts/native-doctor.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
const ok = await native.cli.doctor();
await native.stop();
if (!ok) process.exitCode = 1;   // the consumer script owns the exit code

// scripts/native-clean.ts
import { native } from "../src/native";
await native.start();
await native.cli.clean();        // no target => confirm-gated full projectDir wipe
await native.stop();

Directory roles (gitignore both):
  .moku/tauri/   (projectDir) — the generated Tauri project: gitignored, fully regenerable,
                 never committed. Contains src-tauri/ with tauri.conf.json, Cargo.toml,
                 build.rs, Rust sources, capability JSON, and (after mobileInit) gen/apple|android.
  dist-native/   (outDir) — final packaged artifacts, per target: dist-native/macos/,
                 dist-native/ios/, dist-native/android/, ...

--- Lower-level surfaces (everything cli fronts stays reachable) ---

await native.start();
await native.doctor.run({ target: "ios" });                  // DoctorReport
await native.project.generate({ target: "macos" });          // GenerateResult
const report = native.project.getCompleteness({ target: "android" });
const source = await native.project.ensureIconSource();      // absolute icon source path
await native.build.prepare({ target: "macos" });             // scaffold + codegen + icons
const result = await native.build.run({ target: "macos" });  // BuildResult
const all = await native.build.runAll();                     // sequential, config.targets order
const v = await native.tauri.getVersion();                      // { cliVersion } | undefined
const runner = native.tauri.getRunner();                        // { nodePath, tauriJsPath }
await native.stop();

--- Test seams (all subprocess/render/probe seams injectable) ---

import { createApp, type Tauri, type Doctor, type Cli } from "@moku-labs/native";

const lines: string[] = [];
const app = createApp({
  config: { /* ...valid app/web/system config, temp projectDir/outDir... */ },
  pluginConfigs: {
    tauri: { spawnImpl: fakeSpawn, nodePath: "/usr/bin/node" },  // Tauri.SpawnFn
    doctor: { probeImpl: fakeProbe, probeTimeoutMs: 50 },        // Doctor.ProbeFn
    cli: { renderImpl: line => lines.push(line), confirmImpl: async () => true }
  }
});
// `bun run test` (unit + integration) runs with NO native toolchain installed.
// `bun run test:smoke` is the opt-in real-toolchain proof: it packages a real macOS .app and
// a real iOS simulator .app — the iOS case builds TWICE in the same project dir, which is the
// rebuild proof — inside a fresh mkdtemp workspace, driven purely by web.cwd and
// absolute projectDir/outDir paths (it never chdir's), and skips the iOS case when doctor's
// ios-tools / ios-platform checks do not pass. It composes ALL FIVE capabilities and then
// LAUNCHES the macOS binary for 4s, asserting it is still alive with no panic on stderr
// before terminating that one pid — a tauri.conf.json the plugins cannot deserialize builds
// fine and only fails on the first frame.

====================================================================
12. ERROR HANDLING PATTERNS (as implemented)
====================================================================

House format: every framework error message is "[native] <what happened>." followed by an
indented actionable second line ("  <fix-it / next command>").

(a) Composition-time validation — project.onInit -> validateProjectConfig(ctx.global) throws:
  - "[native] app.name is required." (empty name)
  - '[native] app.identifier "<x>" is not a valid reverse-DNS identifier.'
  - "[native] web.build is required." / web.devCommand / web.devUrl / web.dist (each checked)
  - '[native] app.version "<x>" is not a valid semantic version.' (/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+(?:[-+][\w.]+)?$/
    — it lands raw inside a Cargo TOML string)
  - '[native] app.buildNumber "<x>" is not a valid build number.' (/^[\w.]+$/ — raw in plist/JSON)
  - '[native] signing.android.keystorePasswordEnv "<x>" is not a valid environment variable
    name.' (and keyPasswordEnv — each lands raw inside a Kotlin System.getenv("…") call)
  - '[native] config.projectDir "<x>" resolves outside the project.' (the SAME
    positive-containment rule the destructive clean guard uses, so a projectDir clean() would
    refuse fails at createApp instead of at clean time)
  - '[native] config.outDir "<x>" is a directory this app must not deliver into.' — the LOOSER
    isDeliveryPath rule: outDir is written into and replaced file by file, never recursively
    cleaned, so a CI cache mount outside the checkout is legitimate. Refused: a filesystem
    root, $HOME itself, an ancestor of the cwd or of $HOME.
  - unknown config.system capability names
  - '[native] deep-link is composed in config.system but capabilities["deep-link"].scheme is
    missing.', plus a scheme that is not a valid URL scheme (/^[a-z][a-z\d+.-]*$/i)
  These fire at createApp composition, BEFORE any verb runs. Single owner: only project
  validates; build/doctor/cli have no onInit.

(b) Resolution failures — the tauri seam, before any subprocess:
  - "[native] Could not locate a `node` binary on PATH." + install/version-manager fix-it.
    Raised when ctx.env.get("PATH") yields nothing to walk — the exact failure a replaced
    `pluginConfigs.env.providers` list produces.
  - "[native] Could not resolve `@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js`." + dependency fix-it.

(c) Subprocess failures — tauri one-shot verbs (icon/build/mobileInit) throw TauriError:
  classify(code, scrubbedOutput) matches ordered, most-specific-first regex patterns per
  SIGNAL LINE over BOTH already-scrubbed streams:
    xcode-script-failed: PhaseScriptExecution … Build\ Rust\ Code
    signing-failed:      /codesign|no signing certificate|provisioning profile|notariz|keychain|signtool|jarsigner|keystore/i
    toolchain-missing:   /command not found|xcode-select|android_home|ndk (not found|is not installed)|rustup|cargo: not found/i
    platform-missing:    /is not installed\. Please download and install the platform|Found no destinations/i
    device-unavailable:  /no devices found|device not found|simulator (not booted|not found)|no emulators found|adb: no devices/i
    config-invalid:      /failed to (parse|read) .*tauri\.conf|invalid config|schema validation failed/i
    compile-failed:      /error\[e\d+\]|could not compile|compilation failed/i
  Ordering rationale: xcode-script-failed sits AHEAD of signing-failed and compile-failed (the
  Xcode "Build Rust Code" phase failing is a runner/toolchain problem inside Xcode, and neither
  other fix-it helps); platform-missing sits AHEAD of device-unavailable (a missing iOS SDK
  platform reports both, and only the download fix-it helps); config-invalid is anchored to a
  failure verb so an ordinary tauri.conf.json mention in progress output is not misclassified.
  Lines matching /^\s*Warn\b/ are EXCLUDED from classification entirely — every unsigned iOS
  simulator build prints "Warn No code signing certificates found …".
  No match: kind = "cancelled" when the exit code is null (signal-terminated), else "unknown".
  Only SIGNAL lines are classified: a 50k-line xcodebuild log narrates "CodeSign <path>" and
  exports the whole keychain environment, and one such mention must not decide the taxonomy.
  That makes the signal filter part of the taxonomy's contract: every trigger above must be
  admitted by it, or its bucket is unreachable. "not booted" (device-unavailable) and
  "invalid config" (config-invalid) carry neither an "error" nor a "failed", so both are
  signal triggers in their own right; a table test feeds one real-shaped line per taxonomy
  alternative through classify() to keep that true.
  stderrTail is built as: the LAST 15 de-duplicated SIGNAL lines of the scrubbed output
  (/\berror\b[: ]/, /^\s*Error\b/, panicked, cannot find, not found, no <x> found, not
  installed, not booted, invalid config, PhaseScriptExecution, failed — skipping
  `export …` dumps and *_ERROR build-setting echoes), a "…" separator, then the last 10 lines
  verbatim. A plain "last 20 lines" tail is useless for xcodebuild, where the cause sits
  hundreds of lines above a simulator destination list.

(d) Pipeline failures — build:
  - Each phase emits native:phase "error" (durationMs + the error message as detail) and
    RETHROWS; the next phase never starts. runAll stops at the first failing target.
  - compile/bundle attribute the failure to whichever phase is OPEN.
  - Mobile completeness gate: an "incomplete" gen/ tree throws
    "[native] <target> project tree is incomplete.\n  Missing <files> — run `native doctor`
    to diagnose, or `native clean --target <t>` to reset before rebuilding."
  - collect: zero glob matches throws (never a silent empty success).

(e) Diagnosis — doctor.run never throws on check failures: Promise.allSettled + a
  settled-rejection -> internal-error "fail" CheckResult; a timeout -> "warn". Warns never
  flip report.ok; only "fail" rows do.

(f) Dev sessions:
  - tauri.dev(): a concurrent second call throws "[native] tauri dev already running";
    a readiness-poll timeout rejects `ready` and reaps the process group; stop() never rejects.
    `ready` also rejects the moment the session is over — "[native] dev session stopped before
    the dev server became ready." when stop() was called or the dev process exited first — so
    Ctrl-C or a dev process that died on a taken port never polls out the full window. Each
    probe is bounded by a 2s fetch timeout, and api.ts parks a .catch on `handle.ready` the way
    it does on `exited`, so a caller awaiting only `exited` gets no unhandled rejection.
  - cli.dev(): a signal-terminated exit ({ code: null }) resolves cleanly; a numeric non-zero
    code throws "[native] tauri dev exited with code N."

(g) Destructive operations:
  - clean() calls assertCleanableRoot FIRST:
    '[native] Refusing to clean projectDir "<root>".\n  Set config.projectDir to a dedicated
    subdirectory such as ".moku/tauri".' — POSITIVE containment, not a blacklist: root must
    resolve strictly INSIDE the cwd or the OS temp root and must not be, or contain, the cwd
    or $HOME, nor be a filesystem root. Symlinks are realpath'd and comparison is NFC +
    case-insensitive on darwin/win32. It is a pure predicate and is tested as one.
  - cli.clean() with no target additionally requires a styled confirm.
  - project.clean validates every candidate path against projectDir before deletion; the
    android keystore.properties removal is a single named file, never a recursive remove.
  - project.clearMobileBuildOutput (the other recursive delete) passes assertCleanableRoot
    AND the pure predicate isClearableBuildOutput: the REAL path of gen/apple/build must sit
    strictly inside the real projectDir, so a symlinked build directory is refused with
    '[native] Refusing to remove build output outside projectDir: <real path>.' and never
    followed. Refusals are tested through the predicate on plain strings; the destructive
    function only ever runs against a fresh mkdtemp workspace.
  - build's collect phase REMOVES each destination before copying (fs.cp merges into an
    existing .app), and only after artifactDestination() proved the destination strictly
    inside <outDir>/<target> and that directory strictly inside outDir; otherwise
    '[native] Refusing to collect "<path>" outside <root>.'

(h) Secrets — signing config holds env-var NAMES and identifiers, not values; doctor's signing
  check uses env.has and identity COUNTS only; every subprocess output line (build, dev, and
  errors' stderrTail) passes the entropy-gated scrubber before any log/callback/exception.

====================================================================
13. EXTENSION PATTERNS (custom plugins)
====================================================================

The package root exports `createPlugin` — the consumer-plugin factory bound to this
framework's Config/Events chain. Consumer plugins are passed to createApp({ plugins: [...] }).
Every plugin ctx carries ctx.log and ctx.env (core plugins from @moku-labs/common).

(a) Hook the GLOBAL events — no depends edge needed:

import { createApp, createPlugin } from "@moku-labs/native";
import type { NativeCompleteEvent, NativePhaseEvent } from "@moku-labs/native";

const notifyPlugin = createPlugin("notify", {
  hooks: ctx => ({
    "native:phase": (payload: NativePhaseEvent) => {
      if (payload.status === "error") ctx.log.warn("notify:phase-failed", { ...payload });
    },
    "native:complete": (payload: NativeCompleteEvent) => {
