      ctx.log.info("notify:built", { target: payload.target, outPath: payload.outPath });
    }
  })
});

const native = createApp({ plugins: [notifyPlugin], config: { /* ... */ } });

(b) Hook a PER-PLUGIN event — needs the depends edge for event-type merging:

import { createPlugin, doctorPlugin, type Doctor } from "@moku-labs/native";

const auditPlugin = createPlugin("audit", {
  depends: [doctorPlugin],
  hooks: () => ({
    "doctor:check": (payload: Doctor.CheckResult) => { /* record/forward each check */ }
  })
});

(c) Call upstream APIs — depends + ctx.require:

import { createPlugin, buildPlugin, projectPlugin } from "@moku-labs/native";

const releasePlugin = createPlugin("release", {
  depends: [projectPlugin, buildPlugin],
  api: ctx => ({
    async ship(target: "macos" | "windows" | "linux") {
      const result = await ctx.require(buildPlugin).run({ target });
      ctx.log.info("release:shipped", { artifacts: result.artifacts });
      return result;
    }
  })
});
// createApp({ plugins: [releasePlugin] }) => app.release.ship("macos")

(d) Catch a classified failure by kind — import the class by NAME (the namespaces are
    type-only):

import { TauriError } from "@moku-labs/native";

try {
  await native.cli.build({ target: "ios" });
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TauriError && error.kind === "platform-missing") {
    // run `xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS` and retry
  }
}

(e) Emitting the global events from your own plugin is sanctioned (spec/07 §6), but build is
    the sole emitter by convention — prefer plugin-prefixed custom events for your own domains.

(f) House patterns worth copying from the source:
    - Per-plugin domain context types are core's `PluginCtx<Config, State, Events>` intersected
      with what the plugin really uses (global/log/env/require); `require` is constrained to
      that plugin's real dependencies, so nothing mirrors core's internal registry types.
    - Injectable seams (spawnImpl/probeImpl/renderImpl/confirmImpl) with `undefined` meaning
      "the real implementation" keep 90% coverage reachable without native toolchains.
    - State uses `undefined` for absence (never null), except where a union mirrors a Node
      API surface (DevExit.code/signal) — D-014, which is why getVersion() answers
      `{ cliVersion } | undefined`.
    - `| undefined` is spelled explicitly on optional config fields (exactOptionalPropertyTypes).

====================================================================
14. KEY DESIGN DECISIONS (from .planning/decisions.md)
====================================================================

- D-001: Tiers — project and doctor are Complex (generators/ and checks/ sub-domains);
  tauri, build, cli are Standard.
- D-002: tauri has NO onStop; dev teardown is owned by the dev seam's API control flow
  (process-group spawn, signal handlers, DevHandle.stop()). cli.dev awaits, never holds.
- D-003: native:phase / native:complete are GLOBAL framework events declared in config.ts,
  emitted by build, hooked by cli; doctor:check stays per-plugin.
- D-004: Shared types (Target, MobileTarget, NativePhase, PHASE_ORDER, CapabilityConfigMap,
  AppleSigning, TauriRunner, BuildFlavor) live in src/config.ts; config.ts never imports from
  plugin directories.
- D-005: The substantive config surface is GLOBAL Config; per-plugin configs are minimal knobs.
- D-006: project owns clean (the generated tree's whole lifecycle); cli.clean is a thin,
  confirm-gated delegate.
- D-007: Dependency directions — build -> [project, tauri]; doctor -> [project, tauri];
  cli -> [project, tauri, build, doctor]; project and tauri stay dependency-free.
- D-009: The two-createApp consumer shape is a documented deliverable — see section 11.
- D-011: deep-link is custom-scheme-only in v1 ({ mode: "scheme", scheme }); the mode
  discriminant keeps "universal" additive.
- D-012: v1 mobile permission codegen is conf-only — zero XML patching ships. (EXTENDED: the
  patch pass now also rewrites the Xcode/Android-Studio runner command, because
  Tauri's generated build phase calls a runner that does not resolve inside those IDEs.)
- D-013: tauri CLI invocation is [nodePath, tauriJsPath, verb, ...args] with a PATH-walked
  real node and require.resolve("@tauri-apps/cli/tauri.js"); never bunx/`--bun`/the .node
  addon; node is a hard doctor prerequisite; plain `tauri init` is never used.
- D-014: State nullability — `undefined` is the house norm for absence; `| null` only mirrors
  Node API surfaces. tauri.dev() carries an onOutput render seam for cli.
- D-015: SUPERSEDED. The icons phase was a v1 no-op while no icon-source config field existed.
  `config.app.icon` now exists, `project.ensureIconSource()` supplies a generated placeholder
  when it is unset, and the icons phase really runs `tauri icon`.

====================================================================
15. SIGNING, STORE BUILDS, AND THE iOS SIMULATOR
====================================================================

The rule: CONFIG holds identifiers and env-var NAMES; the ENVIRONMENT holds secrets, and
Tauri/Gradle read them directly. Nothing secret is written to tauri.conf.json, to Gradle, or
to any log line (every subprocess line is scrubbed first).

Environment variables (never config):
| Variable(s) | Used for |
|---|---|
| APPLE_ID + APPLE_PASSWORD + APPLE_TEAM_ID | Notarization with an app-specific password. |
| APPLE_API_KEY + APPLE_API_ISSUER + APPLE_API_KEY_PATH | Notarization with an App Store Connect API key. Either complete set satisfies doctor. |
| APPLE_CERTIFICATE + APPLE_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD | Base64 signing certificate imported into a CI keychain; presence also skips the local keychain probe. |
| <keystorePasswordEnv> / <keyPasswordEnv> | Android release signing, read by Gradle via System.getenv at build time. |

Config -> tauri.conf.json mapping (every key ABSENT when unset; bundle.iOS and bundle.android
stay as empty objects, bundle.macOS is omitted entirely when nothing is configured):
  signing.apple.teamId              -> bundle.iOS.developmentTeam
  signing.apple.signingIdentity     -> bundle.macOS.signingIdentity ("-" = ad-hoc)
  signing.apple.providerShortName   -> bundle.macOS.providerShortName
  signing.apple.entitlements        -> bundle.macOS.entitlements (rebased onto src-tauri)
  signing.apple.appStore === true   -> generates src-tauri/Entitlements.plist
                                       (com.apple.security.app-sandbox +
                                        com.apple.security.network.client) for macOS when
                                       `entitlements` is unset, and points macOS.entitlements at it
  signing.apple.*MinimumSystemVersion -> bundle.{macOS,iOS}.minimumSystemVersion
  signing.apple.exportMethod        -> read by the build plugin, passed to
                                       `tauri ios build --export-method` on DEVICE builds
  app.category                      -> bundle.category
  app.buildNumber                   -> bundle.{iOS,macOS}.bundleVersion

Unsigned dev builds and iOS simulator builds require NO credentials. That is why doctor's
signing check is warn-only: a missing credential never fails a build and never flips report.ok.

iOS simulator builds:
  await native.cli.build({ target: "ios", simulator: true });
  // -> tauri ios build --target aarch64-sim --ci   (x86_64 on an Intel host)
  // -> unsigned gen/apple/build/<slice>/<Product Name>.app, collected to dist-native/ios/
Prerequisites (all diagnosed by `native doctor`, ios scope):
  - rust targets: rustup target add aarch64-apple-ios aarch64-apple-ios-sim   [ios-tools, fail]
  - xcodegen:     brew install xcodegen                                       [ios-tools, fail]
  - cocoapods:    brew install cocoapods                                      [ios-tools, fail]
  - iOS platform: xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS                            [ios-platform, warn]
The first iOS build runs `tauri ios init --ci` once (after tauri.conf.json exists) and then
rewrites the baked-in runner command in gen/apple/project.yml and every
gen/apple/*.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj to the absolute `"<node>" "<tauri.js>"` pair. Without
that rewrite the Xcode "Build Rust Code" phase fails immediately (kind: xcode-script-failed),
because the runner Tauri detected (`node tauri`, `bun tauri`, …) does not resolve inside Xcode.
Rebuilding the SAME tree (no clean in between) needs two more things, both automatic:
  - patchMobile writes CODE_SIGN_ALLOW_ENTITLEMENTS_MODIFICATION into every buildSettings
    block of the pbxproj and each target's settings.base in project.yml — a capability
    plugin's build script rewrites <app>_iOS.entitlements mid-build, which Xcode otherwise
    refuses ("Entitlements file … was modified during the build").
  - the compile phase clears gen/apple/build first — Tauri renames its fresh .app into the
    previous archive and fails with "Directory not empty (os error 66)".
Android needs neither: Gradle owns and reuses its own build tree.
The smoke suite proves it: the iOS case builds the simulator app TWICE in one project dir.

====================================================================
16. BREAKING CHANGES IN THIS RELEASE
====================================================================

| What breaks | Migration |
|---|---|
| web.dev.command / web.dev.url | Use the flat web.devCommand / web.devUrl. Global config is shallow-merged, so a nested `dev` object could never merge cleanly (spec/05 §3). |
| tauri.mobileInit({ platform }) | tauri.mobileInit({ target }). |
| Build/Cli/Doctor/Project/Tauri are TYPE-ONLY namespaces | Import the runtime value by name: `import { TauriError } from "@moku-labs/native"`. |
| Default `targets` is no longer all five | It is hostTargets(process.platform) — one desktop target. Set `targets` explicitly to build ios/android. |
| Project.RegistryRow plugin fields are optional | Null-check npmPackage/crate/crateRange/npmRange/rustInit — the `tray` row is a cargo feature (cargoFeatures: ["tray-icon"]) and carries none of them. |

Also new (non-breaking): config.app.icon/category/buildNumber, config.signing.apple,
config.signing.android.keyPasswordEnv, build.prepare(), project.ensureIconSource(),
project.patchMobile({ runner }), tauri.getRunner(), tauri.build({ simulator, exportMethod, aab }),
doctor's probeTimeoutMs + ios-tools/ios-platform checks, and the hostTargets() helper.

Per-plugin READMEs (deeper narratives): src/plugins/project/README.md,
src/plugins/tauri/README.md, src/plugins/build/README.md, src/plugins/doctor/README.md,
src/plugins/cli/README.md. Moku Core specification:
https://github.com/moku-labs/core/tree/main/specification
